theory.intro: **Percentage change** measures the change as a percentage of the original amount. Subtract to find the change, divide by the original, then multiply by $100$. A positive answer is an increase, a negative answer a decrease.
facts: Always divide by the original amount, never the final amount.
A positive percentage change is an increase; a negative one is a decrease.
Use a positive original amount and the same units for both amounts. A change of zero means no percentage change.
steps: Divide by the original amount and multiply by $100$.
State the result as an increase (positive) or a decrease (negative).

workedExamples.question_text:
Find the percentage change:
(a) $175$ changes to $203$.
(b) $96$ changes to $78$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=203-175\\&=28\\\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{28}{175}\times100\\&=16\%\end{align*}$
This is a $16\%$ increase.

(b)
$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=78-96\\&=-18\\\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{-18}{96}\times100\\&=-18.75\%\end{align*}$
This is an $18.75\%$ decrease.

workedExamples.question_text: A ticket price changes from $\$87$ to $\$52$. Find the percentage change, correct to $2$ decimal places.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=52-87\\&=-35\\\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{-35}{87}\times100\\&\approx-40.23\%\end{align*}$
This is a $40.23\%$ decrease, to $2$ decimal places.

workedExamples.question_text:
Find the percentage change when a price of $\$68$ is increased:
(a) to $\$85$
(b) by $\$85$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Increased to $\$85$ gives the final price.
$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=85-68\\&=17\\\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{17}{68}\times100\\&=25\%\end{align*}$
This is a $25\%$ increase.

(b) Increased by $\$85$ gives the change.
$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{85}{68}\times100\\&=125\%\end{align*}$
This is a $125\%$ increase.
The final price is $\$68+\$85=\$153$.

workedExamples.question_text: A price changes from $\$72$ to $\$93$, then back to $\$72$. Find each percentage change, correct to $2$ decimal places. Explain why they differ.
workedExamples.solution_text:
From $\$72$ to $\$93$:
$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=93-72\\&=21\\\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{21}{72}\times100\\&\approx29.17\%\end{align*}$
This is a $29.17\%$ increase.

From $\$93$ to $\$72$:
$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=72-93\\&=-21\\\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{-21}{93}\times100\\&\approx-22.58\%\end{align*}$
This is a $22.58\%$ decrease.
The change amount has the same size, but the original amount is different for each calculation. This is why the percentages differ.

workedExamples.question_text:
Find the percentage change when a price of $\$80$ is decreased:
(a) by $\$24$
(b) to $\$24$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Decreased by $\$24$ means the change is $-\$24$.
$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{-24}{80}\times100\\&=-30\%\end{align*}$
This is a $30\%$ decrease.

(b) Decreased to $\$24$ gives the final price.
$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=24-80\\&=-56\\\text{Percentage change}&=\dfrac{-56}{80}\times100\\&=-70\%\end{align*}$
This is a $70\%$ decrease.

Last year a tennis club had $150$ members.
This year it has $126$ members.
Find the percentage change in membership.

Last year a book club had $60$ members.
This year it has $96$ members.
Find the percentage change in membership.

The population of a town changes from $8500$ to $9350$.
Find the percentage change.

A ticket was $\$60$ but changed to $\$29$.
Find the percentage change, correct to $2$ decimal places.
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{29-60}{60}\times100$
$=\dfrac{-31}{60}\times100$
$\approx-51.67\%$
This is a $51.67\%$ decrease, to $2$ decimal places.

mastery.question_text:
A price of $\$12$ is increased by $\$15$.
Find the percentage change.
mastery.solution_text:
Increased by $\$15$ means the change is $\$15$ and the original is $\$12$.
$\dfrac{15}{12}\times100$
$=125\%$ increase

mastery.question_text:
A quantity changes from $83$ to $47$.
Find the percentage change, correct to $1$ decimal place.
mastery.solution_text:
$\dfrac{47-83}{83}\times100$
$=\dfrac{-36}{83}\times100$
$\approx-43.4\%$
This is a $43.4\%$ decrease, to $1$ decimal place.
